questions.q: Why doesn't a dashboard built for a wide desktop canvas automatically work well on a phone?
options: Columns collapse into unreadably narrow strips, text becomes too small, and touch targets end up too close together for a finger instead of a precise mouse pointer
Tableau dashboards physically cannot be viewed on a phone at all
Phone screens cannot display any charts, only text
Desktop dashboards automatically convert to mobile with zero changes needed
questions.explain: A layout designed for a wide screen (e.g. a four-column KPI row) doesn't hold up when squeezed onto a phone — text, spacing, and touch targets all need to be rethought, not just shrunk.

questions.q: What does a device-specific layout let you do?
options: Define an alternate arrangement (for Phone, Tablet, or a custom size) of the same underlying worksheets and objects, without rebuilding the content itself
Create an entirely separate workbook with duplicated worksheets for each device
Restrict a dashboard so it can only ever be viewed on one specific device
Automatically convert all Tableau dashboards into a mobile app
questions.explain: A device-specific layout reuses the exact same worksheets and objects from the Default (desktop) layout — you're only rearranging and resizing which pieces show and in what order, not rebuilding content.

questions.q: What does Auto-Generate Layout actually produce, according to this lesson?
options: A useful first-pass phone arrangement, stacking existing objects vertically — a starting point, not a finished result
A pixel-perfect, fully finished mobile layout requiring no further adjustment
A completely blank layout with no objects at all
An automatic conversion of the dashboard into a PDF
questions.explain: Auto-Generate Layout stacks objects vertically in roughly their desktop order, scaled to phone width — genuinely useful as a starting point, but it rarely produces a finished mobile design on its own.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend switching Hover-triggered actions to Select when building a phone layout?
options: There's no hover on a touchscreen — a finger either taps (selects) or it doesn't rest in place the way a mouse pointer can
Select triggers are faster to configure than Hover triggers in every case
Hover triggers are not supported anywhere in Tableau, on any device
Phone layouts disable all dashboard actions automatically
questions.explain: Hover depends on a pointer resting on a mark, which doesn't exist on a touchscreen. Select (tap) is the trigger that actually makes sense for a phone layout.

questions.q: What is the single most important rule this lesson gives for designing a phone layout?
options: A phone layout is a different information hierarchy, not a scaled-down desktop layout — decide what a phone viewer actually needs first and build outward from that
A phone layout should always contain exactly the same number of objects as the desktop layout
Phone layouts should never include any charts, only KPI numbers
Phone layouts must be built before the desktop layout exists
questions.explain: The lesson's core point: don't start from the desktop version and shrink everything until it technically fits. Decide what matters most to a phone viewer (usually the headline number and maybe one chart) and build from there.
